answer: Burst-proof islands resist sybils. Each agent joins one island with a fixed quota. Each epoch its coordinator broadcasts a task sealed under an ephemeral cipher. Every agent fans the task across local workers and must return all results within 500 ms, a window software timers cannot arbitrate, so stamps must come from the machine's crystal clock. Honest agents pay once. An attacker with N puppets needs N dedicated multi-core workers, as challenges fire simultaneously and shared hardware misses deadlines; costs scale with N every epoch, so fakes lose money.
